title: The imparfait
description: Describe how things were, what you used to do, and what was going on.
rule: Form the imparfait from the nous form of the present: drop -ons and add -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient (nous finissons → je finissais, nous prenons → je prenais, nous avons → j’avais). Être is the only exception: its stem is ét- (j’étais, nous étions). Verbs in -ger keep an e before a (je mangeais, ils mangeaient) but not before i (nous mangions, vous mangiez); verbs in -cer write ç before a (je commençais) but c before i (nous commencions). Use the imparfait to describe a scene or situation in the past (il faisait beau, la maison était grande) and for past habits, often with tous les étés, d’habitude or autrefois. Use it too for age, feelings and states (j’avais dix ans, elle était fatiguée) and for an action that was in progress (je lisais).
example: Quand j’étais petit, nous allions à la mer tous les étés. · Il faisait beau et je lisais dans le jardin.
aside: The imparfait covers English “used to”, “was …-ing” and plain “was”: je lisais can mean I was reading or I used to read.

exercises.source: parler · tu · imparfait
exercises.hint: Start from nous parlons, drop -ons, then add the ending for tu.
exercises.feedback: Tu takes the same ending as je.
exercises.explanation: Nous parlons gives the stem parl-. Tu takes -ais: tu parlais.

exercises.source: Quand nous étions petits, nous ____ souvent au parc.
exercises.hint: Match the ending to the subject nous.
exercises.feedback: Each person has its own ending. Find the one that goes with nous.
exercises.explanation: Nous takes -ions: nous jouions. -iez is for vous, -aient for ils and elles, -ais for je and tu.

exercises.source: Mes grands-parents ____ (habiter) à la campagne.
exercises.hint: Mes grands-parents can be replaced by ils. Which ending goes with ils?
exercises.feedback: The subject is plural, so it needs the plural ending.
exercises.explanation: The stem habit- comes from nous habitons. A plural subject takes -aient: habitaient. The -ent is silent.

exercises.source: Le soir, vous regardais la télé.
answers: Le soir, vous regardiez la télé.
exercises.hint: Look at the subject: vous.
exercises.feedback: The ending -ais belongs to je and tu, not to vous.
exercises.explanation: Vous takes -iez in the imparfait: vous regardiez.

exercises.source: They (feminine) were listening to the radio.
exercises.hint: Elles is plural.
exercises.feedback: Choose the verb tile whose ending matches elles.
exercises.explanation: Elles takes -aient: elles écoutaient. Écoutait is the form for il or elle.

exercises.source: finir · je · imparfait
exercises.hint: Start from the nous form of the present: nous finissons.
exercises.feedback: Keep the whole nous stem, including -iss-.
exercises.explanation: Nous finissons gives the stem finiss-, and je takes -ais: je finissais.

exercises.source: Autrefois, mon père ____ du thé le matin.
exercises.hint: What is the nous form of boire in the present?
exercises.feedback: The stem comes from the nous form, not from ils or from the infinitive.
exercises.explanation: Nous buvons gives the stem buv-, so il buvait. Boiv- comes from ils boivent, and buvaient is the plural form.

exercises.source: Le dimanche, tu ____ (faire) du vélo avec ton frère.
exercises.hint: Nous faisons gives the stem.
exercises.feedback: Build the form on the nous stem, then add the tu ending.
exercises.explanation: Nous faisons gives fais-, and tu takes -ais: tu faisais.

exercises.instruction: Put the verb in the imparfait.
exercises.source: Nous lisons le journal.
exercises.hint: Keep the stem of nous lisons and change only the ending.
exercises.feedback: In the imparfait the nous ending is not -ons.
exercises.explanation: Nous lisons gives the stem lis-, and nous takes -ions: nous lisions.

exercises.source: Je finisais mes devoirs à cinq heures.
answers: Je finissais mes devoirs à cinq heures.
exercises.hint: Compare the verb with nous finissons.
exercises.feedback: Part of the nous stem is missing.
exercises.explanation: Finir keeps -iss- from nous finissons: je finissais.

exercises.instruction: Translate into French. Use the imparfait.
exercises.source: You used to drink a lot of milk. (to a friend)

alternatives.answer: Tu avais l’habitude de boire beaucoup de lait.
alternatives.message: That is correct French, but this exercise practises the imparfait of boire itself: tu buvais.

exercises.hint: Used to describes a habit. Think of nous buvons.
exercises.feedback: Check the stem of boire and the ending for tu.
exercises.explanation: A past habit takes the imparfait. Nous buvons gives buv-, so tu buvais.

exercises.source: être · nous · imparfait
exercises.hint: Être does not follow the nous-stem rule. It has a special stem.
exercises.feedback: Nous sommes cannot give the stem. Use the special stem of être.
exercises.explanation: Être is the only exception: its stem is ét-, so nous étions.

exercises.source: Quand mon frère ____ petit, il voulait être pompier.
exercises.hint: The subject is mon frère, which is like il, and être has its own stem.
exercises.feedback: Check both the special stem of être and the ending for il.
exercises.explanation: Être uses the stem ét-, and mon frère (il) takes -ait: mon frère était. Sommait is built wrongly on nous sommes.

exercises.source: Nous sommions contents de te voir.
answers: Nous étions contents de te voir.
exercises.hint: Être is the exception to the nous-stem rule.
exercises.feedback: The imparfait of être is not built on nous sommes.
exercises.explanation: The imparfait stem of être is ét-: nous étions.

exercises.source: En juillet, vous ____ (être) en vacances, non ?
exercises.hint: Use the special stem of être and the vous ending.
exercises.feedback: Start with the stem ét- and add the ending for vous.
exercises.explanation: Ét- plus -iez gives vous étiez.

exercises.instruction: Translate into French. Use the imparfait.
exercises.source: They (masculine) were at school.
exercises.hint: Être has a special stem. Add the plural ending.
exercises.feedback: Check the stem of être and the ending for ils.
exercises.explanation: Ét- plus -aient gives ils étaient. À plus l’école stays à l’école.

exercises.source: We were very tired.
exercises.hint: Être does not use nous sommes as its stem.
exercises.feedback: One verb tile is built on the wrong stem.
exercises.explanation: The imparfait of être is nous étions. Sommions does not exist.

exercises.source: manger · je · imparfait
exercises.hint: Before the letter a, the g needs help to stay soft.
exercises.feedback: Without an extra letter, the g would sound hard before a.
exercises.explanation: Nous mangeons keeps an e after the g, so je mangeais keeps it too.

exercises.source: commencer · nous · imparfait
exercises.hint: Before the letter i, does the c need a cedilla?
exercises.feedback: The cedilla is only needed before a, o and u.
exercises.explanation: C already sounds like s before i, so there is no ç: nous commencions.

exercises.source: Quand nous étions enfants, nous ____ dans le lac.
exercises.hint: Before the i of -ions, is the extra e needed?
exercises.feedback: The g of nager only needs an e before a or o. Check the subject too.
exercises.explanation: G is already soft before i, so nous nagions has no e. Nageaient and nageais keep the e but belong to other persons.

exercises.source: Au lycée, le cours ____ (commencer) toujours à huit heures.
exercises.hint: The ending for il begins with the letter a.
exercises.feedback: Before a, the c needs a mark to keep its s sound.
exercises.explanation: Before a, c becomes ç to stay soft: le cours commençait.

exercises.instruction: Fix the spelling of the verb.
exercises.source: Ils mangaient au restaurant le samedi.
answers: Ils mangeaient au restaurant le samedi.
exercises.hint: Say mangaient aloud. Is the g soft?
exercises.feedback: A -ger verb needs an extra letter before a.
exercises.explanation: Before a, -ger verbs keep the e of nous mangeons: ils mangeaient.

exercises.instruction: Put the verb in the imparfait.
exercises.source: Tu voyages beaucoup.
exercises.hint: Voyager is a -ger verb, like manger.
exercises.feedback: Check the letter between the g and the ending.
exercises.explanation: Nous voyageons keeps the e before the ending -ais: tu voyageais.

exercises.instruction: Fix the spelling of the verb.
exercises.source: Elle lancait la balle au chien.
answers: Elle lançait la balle au chien.
exercises.hint: The ending for elle begins with the letter a.
exercises.feedback: As written, the c would sound like k.
exercises.explanation: Before a, c becomes ç to keep its s sound: elle lançait.

exercises.instruction: Translate into French. Use the imparfait.
exercises.source: It was cold. (the weather)
exercises.hint: Weather is described with il and the verb faire.
exercises.feedback: French does not use être for the weather.
exercises.explanation: Weather in a past description uses il faisait: il faisait froid.

exercises.instruction: Translate into French. Use the imparfait.
exercises.source: The house was big.
exercises.hint: Maison is feminine. This is a description, so use être.
exercises.feedback: Check the imparfait of être and the agreement of the adjective.
exercises.explanation: A description in the past takes the imparfait: la maison était grande, with grande agreeing with maison.

exercises.source: Dans le jardin, il y ____ (avoir) beaucoup de fleurs.
exercises.hint: Il y a becomes il y + the imparfait of avoir in a past description.
exercises.feedback: Use the stem of nous avons and the il ending.
exercises.explanation: Il y avait means there was or there were: nous avons gives av-, plus -ait.

exercises.source: Le ciel ____ gris et il pleuvait.
exercises.hint: The subject is le ciel, one thing.
exercises.feedback: Match the ending to a singular subject.
exercises.explanation: Le ciel is like il, so the ending is -ait: était. Été is a past participle, not a conjugated form.

exercises.source: It was raining and it was cold.
answers: Il pleuvait et il faisait froid.
exercises.hint: Weather verbs take il.
exercises.feedback: One verb tile has the wrong ending for il.
exercises.explanation: Pleuvoir and faire for the weather use il: il pleuvait, il faisait froid.

exercises.instruction: Put the description in the imparfait.
exercises.source: La cuisine est petite et sombre.
answers: La cuisine était petite et sombre.
exercises.hint: Change only the verb.
exercises.feedback: Use the special imparfait stem of être.
exercises.explanation: A past description takes the imparfait: la cuisine était petite et sombre.

exercises.instruction: Put the verb in the imparfait to describe a past habit.
exercises.source: Tous les étés, nous allons à la mer.
answers: Tous les étés, nous allions à la mer.
exercises.hint: Aller looks irregular, but nous allons gives a regular stem.
exercises.feedback: Use the nous stem and the nous ending of the imparfait.
exercises.explanation: A repeated past action takes the imparfait. Nous allons gives all-, plus -ions: nous allions.

exercises.instruction: Translate into French. Use the imparfait.
exercises.source: She used to work in a bank.

alternatives.answer: Elle avait l’habitude de travailler dans une banque.
alternatives.message: That is correct French, but this exercise practises the imparfait of travailler itself: elle travaillait.

exercises.hint: Used to describes a habit.
exercises.feedback: French has no separate word for used to; the tense carries it.
exercises.explanation: The imparfait expresses a past habit: elle travaillait dans une banque.

exercises.source: D’habitude, je me ____ (lever) à sept heures.
exercises.hint: Start from nous levons and add the je ending.
exercises.feedback: The stem comes from nous levons, so there is no accent.
exercises.explanation: D’habitude signals a habit. Nous levons gives lev-, plus -ais: je me levais.

exercises.source: Autrefois, les enfants ____ à l’école à pied.
exercises.hint: Les enfants can be replaced by ils.
exercises.feedback: The stem of aller in the imparfait comes from nous allons.
exercises.explanation: Les enfants is plural: ils allaient. Vaient is not a form of aller.

exercises.instruction: Build the French sentence with on.
exercises.source: In the old days, we used to go out often.
exercises.hint: On takes the same ending as il.
exercises.feedback: On means we here, but its verb ending is singular.
exercises.explanation: On takes the il ending -ait: on sortait. Autrefois marks a past habit.

exercises.source: Chaque été, mes cousins venait chez nous.
answers: Chaque été, mes cousins venaient chez nous.
exercises.hint: Mes cousins is plural.
exercises.feedback: The ending does not match the subject.
exercises.explanation: A plural subject takes -aient: mes cousins venaient.

exercises.source: I was ten years old.
exercises.hint: French uses avoir for age.
exercises.feedback: Age is not expressed with être in French.
exercises.explanation: Age in the past takes the imparfait of avoir: j’avais dix ans.

exercises.source: Après sa longue journée, Julie ____ (être) très fatiguée.
exercises.hint: Tiredness is a state. Être has a special stem.
exercises.feedback: Use the stem ét- and the ending for elle.
exercises.explanation: A state in the past takes the imparfait: Julie était très fatiguée.

exercises.source: Quand nous ____ vingt ans, nous habitions à Paris.
exercises.hint: Which verb expresses age in French?
exercises.feedback: Check the verb used for age, then the ending for nous.
exercises.explanation: Age uses avoir: nous avions vingt ans. Étions is the wrong verb, aviez the wrong person, and avons the present.

exercises.instruction: Put both verbs in the imparfait.
exercises.source: Tu as faim et tu es triste.
answers: Tu avais faim et tu étais triste.
exercises.hint: Avoir follows the nous-stem rule. Être does not.
exercises.feedback: Change both verbs, and use the special stem for être.
exercises.explanation: Hunger and sadness are states: tu avais faim, from nous avons, and tu étais, from the stem ét-.

exercises.source: avoir · je · imparfait
exercises.hint: Start from nous avons.
exercises.feedback: Use the stem av- and the je ending. Remember the elision of je.
exercises.explanation: Nous avons gives av-, plus -ais: j’avais.

exercises.source: Mon frère avaient peur des chiens.
answers: Mon frère avait peur des chiens.
exercises.hint: Mon frère is one person.
exercises.feedback: The ending is plural, but the subject is not.
exercises.explanation: Mon frère is like il, so the ending is -ait: il avait peur.

exercises.source: I was reading.
exercises.hint: Was …-ing describes an action in progress.
exercises.feedback: French has no separate -ing form here. Use the imparfait of lire.
exercises.explanation: An action in progress in the past takes the imparfait: je lisais. J’étais en train de lire says the same thing.

exercises.source: The children were sleeping.
answers: Les enfants étaient en train de dormir.
exercises.hint: Were …-ing describes an action in progress.
exercises.feedback: Use one verb in the imparfait, with the ending for a plural subject.
exercises.explanation: An action in progress takes the imparfait: les enfants dormaient. Étaient en train de dormir is also correct.

exercises.source: Hier à minuit, tu ____ déjà.
exercises.hint: The subject is tu.
exercises.feedback: Check the stem from nous dormons and the tu ending.
exercises.explanation: Nous dormons gives dorm-, and tu takes -ais: tu dormais. Dormissais wrongly copies finir.

exercises.source: Hier à midi, nous ____ (préparer) le repas.
exercises.hint: An action in progress at a moment in the past. Match the ending to nous.
exercises.feedback: The nous ending in the imparfait is not -ons.
exercises.explanation: At noon the action was in progress: nous préparions, with the ending -ions.

exercises.instruction: Say the same thing with the imparfait of écrire instead of être en train de.
exercises.source: Elle était en train d’écrire une lettre.
exercises.hint: Nous écrivons gives the stem.
exercises.feedback: Use one verb: écrire in the imparfait, with the ending for elle.
exercises.explanation: The imparfait alone shows an action in progress: nous écrivons gives écriv-, so elle écrivait.

exercises.source: My father was reading the newspaper.
exercises.hint: Mon père is like il.
exercises.feedback: One verb tile has the ending for je or tu.
exercises.explanation: Mon père takes the il ending: lisait, from nous lisons.
